saints.name: St. Ludger
saints.title: Bishop, Apostle of Saxony
saints.shortBlurb: A Frisian disciple of Alcuin who evangelized the Saxons and Frisians and became the first bishop of Münster…
biography: Born about 742 at Zuilen near Utrecht of a noble Frisian family, Ludger was sent to the cathedral school of Gregory at Utrecht and later crossed to York, where he was ordained deacon and studied under Alcuin. Ordained priest at Cologne in 777, he was charged with the missions of East Frisia, centered on Dokkum, where Boniface had been martyred.

When the Saxon leader Widukind drove out the missionaries in 784, Ludger withdrew to Rome and Monte Cassino; recalled to the field, he declined the bishopric of Trier in 793 to evangelize the Saxons. About 800 he founded the abbey of Werden, and at Mimigernaford he built a monastery of canons around which the city of Münster grew.

Consecrated first bishop of Münster on 30 March 805, he converted more by gentleness, men said, than Charlemagne did by force. He died at Billerbeck on 26 March 809, having preached and celebrated Mass twice that day, and was buried at Werden.
saints.knownFor: Evangelizing the Saxons and founding the see of Münster.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 26 March
